correctness.rationale:
Cassini gives \(u^2-uv-v^2=-1\). The congruences \(u^3\equiv v^3\equiv1\pmod m\) yield \((u-1)^2\equiv3(u-1)\equiv0\pmod m\); at \(p
e3\) this forces \(u\equiv1\), and at \(p=3\) the lifting and norm expansion do likewise. Consequently \(m=\gcd(u-1,3(v-1))\); writing \(\delta=v-1\) gives \(3\delta\equiv\delta^2\equiv0\pmod m\). This makes every cubic shift difference vanish modulo \(m\), with the first two differences having exact gcd \(m\). The first-window identity \(4S_0=(v-1)^2(v+2)+a(a^2+3)\) holds by two-step induction. If \(6
mid k\), \(m\) is odd and divides \(S_0\). If \(6\mid k\), the Fibonacci matrix modulo \(8\) gives \(
u_2(m)=t\ge2\) and \(
u_2(S_0)=t-1\), so the gcd is exactly \(m/2\). All quantifiers are proved symbolically; the checker additionally tests \(k=2,4,\ldots,600\) and 7,500 example windows.

originality.rationale: The nearest primary paper explicitly prints the opposite case split as an open cubic conjecture; the new statement is mathematically incompatible with those branches, and its complete unrestricted modular proof is not supplied there. Other materially inspected primary results treat first powers, even-index cubic power sums, selected two-term power-sum prime factors, or divisibility of Lucas power differences, none of which implies the exact all-starting-index window gcd. Targeted mathematical-record searches yielded unrelated cubic reciprocal sums and Lucas period results, not dominating coverage. Possible unindexed or uninspected implicit equivalents remain a stated risk.
residual_risks: The swapped branches may be an editorial error, and a later corrected formulation could exist outside the sources inspected.
The Clary–Hemenway 1993 chapter was examined only at abstract level, so an implicit equivalent in its full text cannot be ruled out.
Indexed mathematical-search coverage is incomplete; priority and novelty need independent bibliographic checking.

value.rationale: The problem is explicitly motivated by published Question 6.1 about third-power Fibonacci window gcds. A complete corrected all-even classification resolves the natural Fibonacci subproblem, exposes the swapped case conditions with concrete counterexamples and proves a nontrivial norm-based simplification of the gcd; it is not merely a numerical correction or a routine parameter substitution. Further work on Lucas cubes, higher powers and general initial values is naturally motivated.
